purpose: Replace the uniform frontal comb with explicit micro-clumps, a graded scalp density foundation and physically based melanin fibers, then remove the progressive-darkening impression without changing the accepted skin response.

ownership.geometry: Aevrynd-authored procedural curves derived from the owned v249 body and r345 technical node

r367.change: Reorganized 968 frontal overlay fibers into 22 overlapping micro-clumps.
r367.finding: The grouping is explicit, but the result still reads as parallel drawn lines at review distance.

r368.change: Added a head-bound density attribute with a 22 mm hairline gradient and reduced density at the center part.
r368.finding: A 0.42 maximum alpha leaves the crown foundation too weak; 0.84 creates a dark cap.

r369.change: Selected a 0.63 density maximum and converted the fibers to Principled Hair BSDF melanin response.
r369.finding: Brown value variation improves, but the dense root layer increases perceived facial darkness.

r370.change: Separated primary, secondary and hairline radii while retaining 525 guides, 8,925 fill curves and 1,090 transition curves.
r370.finding: Fiber hierarchy is clearer and the rear opening remains closed, but the frontal flow and bob perimeter remain too uniform.

r371.change: Reduced scalp density maximum from 0.63 to 0.50 and melanin from 0.76 to 0.68 while holding the review rig at 8 W.
r371.finding: Central skin luminance is unchanged within 0.001%; the matched-camera forehead/hairline region is 0.497% brighter. Perceived darkening is corrected without changing skin material or exposure.

failures: Hairline micro-clumps still resolve as regularly spaced strokes.
Side and rear lengths form an overly straight procedural curtain.
Large-scale locks and local density transitions are not authored strongly enough.
The result lacks natural breakup at the temples, crown and ends.

nextRequiredWork: Author nonparallel surface-following frontal locks and irregular macro silhouettes before adding more fiber density. Preserve the r371 contrast and collision baselines.
